Rule of thumb: call it flat when the period-over-period drop stays under about 1 to 2 percentage points for three or more periods in a row, ideally across several cohorts rather than just one. Also check the level it flattens at, since a flat curve at a low level is still a retention problem.
Action: none needed; send me a curve and I'll apply the test to it.

I don't have last night's Raptors score and I won't guess at it.
Action: look up the final score and top performers, then send it over so you can pass it to Sam.

Here's a draft, not posted: 'Team, the beta passed 10,000 payouts this week. That's down to the care each of you put into it, and it's worth pausing to enjoy. Thank you, I'm proud to be building this with you.' It's warm without being over the top, and short enough to post as is.
Action: wait for your edits, then save it ready for you to post tomorrow.

Plain COUNTIF is enough: =COUNTIF(D:D,">10000") counts payouts over $10,000. Use ">=10000" if exactly $10,000 should count too, and only reach for COUNTIFS if you need a second condition like a date range.
Action: none; paste it into a spare cell, and tell me if you want a second condition added.

Your notes say you picked Lisbon partly for the mild December weather, 12-15 C, and because it's very walkable, so pack layers, a warm jacket for evenings and comfortable walking shoes. That's all the weather detail I have, nothing specific to New Year's Eve itself.
Action: open your note 'Dec 2026 holiday - options' (n-3982) to see if it has NYE plans, and check the Lisbon forecast closer to the trip.

Yes to Hannah for Saturday 1 to 4, I'll let her know. For a rainy afternoon indoors: a Lego build-off where they swap and name each other's creations, a cushion obstacle course with a timer, a house scavenger hunt, then a movie to wind down before pickup.
Action: text Hannah yes, put Jun's 1 to 4 slot on the calendar, and save the activity plan; want me to print the scavenger hunt clues?

Pastel de nata comes from Lisbon, specifically the Belem neighbourhood, where monks at the Jeronimos Monastery made them, and a nearby bakery took over the recipe in the 1830s. Pasteis de Belem still sells them today, which makes a good story for Leo.
Action: none needed; I can find a kid-friendly video or a simple recipe if he wants to try making them.

He's clearly running a very small collections department, and he's persistent. Is it dinner or a walk he thinks he's owed?
Action: nothing queued; tell me if you want a reminder for his next meal or walk.

I don't know the Withrow rink's conditions for Saturday afternoon, so I'll check rather than guess.
Action: look up the City's Withrow Park rink status and hours plus the Saturday afternoon forecast, check the family calendar for Saturday after Leo's swim, and report back.

Playlist coming for tomorrow with Khruangbin and A. R. Rahman instrumentals. For the calendar I'll remove spin and add strength training at the Leslieville YMCA, Tuesdays and Thursdays at 6:15 am, with a hard stop so you're home by 7:15. One conflict: my notes have your run with Marcus on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 6:30 am, the same mornings, so I'll leave that alone until you tell me whether to drop or move it.
Action: build the playlist, find and delete the spin events, add the recurring Tue/Thu 6:15 YMCA block, and ask you about the Marcus run.

Done, I'll put it in a note she can use: no increase above the 2.1% guideline for 2026 without LTB approval, 90 days' written notice on Form N1 and only once every 12 months, and if she gets an N1 for 9% with no LTB application she can pay just the guideline amount.
Action: write the note with links to the official LTB and Ontario pages, and show it to you before you send it to Tanvi.

On it. Old Navy needs a login to unsubscribe, so I'll leave it for your saved list in Notes / Inbox cleanup; Wayfair, Uber Eats promos and Lululemon I'll unsubscribe through their links. The Dyson one you never signed up for I'll check isn't phishing and mark as spam rather than click through. I'll archive the existing promo mail from all five, skip order and receipt emails, and show you any email-based unsubscribe draft before anything is sent.
Action: run the unsubscribes and archive, then report what went through and add Old Navy to the login list.

Pulling your blocked Linear tickets now.
Action: list the tickets assigned to you in a blocked state with what each is blocked on, so you can pick which to clear before next week's standup.

I'll build the cart for all 12 items: milk, eggs, bread, rice, pasta, bananas, apples, yogurt tubes, cheddar, dish soap, paper towels and the frozen veggie dumplings. I'll hold off on checkout so you can see the total and slot options first, and the Sandbanks permit stays paused until you've talked to Sam about PEC.
Action: build the grocery cart, show you the total and pickup or delivery options, and wait for your go before ordering.

That's a big deal: leading your first project end to end as a senior PM, and watching Instant Payouts actually work in May 2026, is worth saying out loud. Congratulations, you earned it.
Action: nothing needed; I can save this as a note for your next review conversation if you'd like.

Quick check: turning it off tomorrow morning and changing the message pull in two directions, so do you want it fully off, or running with the new text? The new text I'd use is: 'Hi, I'm back but still catching up, so replies may be slower than usual. Thanks for your patience.'
Action: update the saved message now and end the out-of-office tomorrow morning unless you tell me to keep it running.

Reminder set for 17:15 for the Shoppers pickup. On the 1:1: my notes have it weekly on Thursdays at 14:00, and since Tom owns the series I may not be able to edit his recurrence, so I'll end the Thursday repeats on your copy from January and add a weekly Wednesday 11:30 1:1 in its place.
Action: set the 17:15 reminder, update your copy of the 1:1 to Wednesdays at 11:30, and check it matches Tom's updated invite.

Booking the onboarding design review with Aisha and Diego for Thu 26 Nov, 10:00 to 10:25, with the agenda in the invite: KYC retry screens, empty states, open questions. I'll check all three calendars first and tell you if there's a clash. Halloween stays open for whenever you're back to it.
Action: check Aisha's and Diego's availability, then send the invite with the agenda in Toronto time.

Not sure yet, so I'll check. Dr. Lin's office moved to Danforth Smiles on Danforth Ave in March 2026, so any confirmations may have come from a new sender or gone to the old Queen East Dental address.
Action: search your email and texts for November appointment confirmations for you and Leo from Danforth Smiles (and the old office); if there are none, I'll give you their number, 416-555-0144, or draft a request for you to approve.

Here's what's left for Halloween night: the costume (tell me what he's going as and I'll make a parts list), the evening plan (who's walking with him, what time you head out, who covers the door), safety gear like reflective tape or a glow stick and a small flashlight, and treats for the door if you're handing out.
Action: check your calendar for Halloween night and build the parts list as soon as you tell me the costume.

Three days late calls for a properly ridiculous mug, and the tradition makes it easy. I'll look for the silliest options that can reach Vancouver fast and bring you the best candidates with delivery dates, and I'll check with you before ordering.
Action: search for ridiculous mugs with fast delivery to Vancouver and report the top picks with prices and arrival dates; I'll also check whether I have Kabir's address.

Booking it: 25 minutes with Aisha and Diego next week, in the morning, with the agenda in the invite: 1) empty-state copy, 2) loading skeleton, 3) who owns the Looker link. I'll also set a hydro payment reminder ahead of the Tue 3 Feb due date.
Action: find a morning next week when all three of you are free, send the invite with the agenda, and set the hydro reminder for the day before it's due.

Here's a draft: 'Hi neighbours! We're having a street yard sale on Sat 4 Oct from 9 to 1, with Sun 5 Oct as the rain date. Please set up tables on your own driveways, and no early birds before 9, we mean it. See you out there!'
Action: wait for your edits, then it's ready for you to paste into the group chat.

I don't have tonight's Leafs schedule in front of me, so I'll check the puck drop time rather than guess.
Action: look up tonight's Leafs game start time and channel, and tell you whether it works for watching after Leo's in bed.

A few fits for single, architect, bikes and old buildings: Little Portugal or Trinity Bellwoods (Victorian rowhouses, Dundas and Ossington bike lanes), the Annex (big old houses, the Bloor bike lane, near U of T), Cabbagetown (the best-preserved Victorian streets, a short ride to the core), and Corktown/Distillery if she likes converted lofts. I'd start with Little Portugal/Trinity Bellwoods or the Annex. I hope her cousin picks up, and I can draft a message to your mom whenever you want.
Action: none; send me the firm's address if you want bike-time checks for each area.

My pick is Brijwasi Sweets: Rs 1,450 plus Rs 120 delivery, the best freshness reviews, and same day if it's ordered before 14:00 IST. I won't order until I have your mom's delivery address and your go-ahead.
Action: ask you for her address and a message for the box, then place the Brijwasi order once you confirm.

A TFSA is after-tax money that grows and comes out tax-free, while an RRSP gives you a deduction now and you pay tax when you withdraw. RRSP tends to win if your income now is higher than it will be in retirement, TFSA if it's the other way around or you want flexible access.
Action: none; give me your income and goals and I can run a comparison for you and Sam.

I'll search for 3 nights in Drumheller during March break, taking 'the week of the 16th' as starting Mon 16 Mar, so tell me if you want different nights. I don't know Tyrrell's ticket prices offhand and they depend on Leo's age bracket, so I'll pull them from the museum's own site.
Action: search family-friendly Drumheller hotels for 3 nights from Mon 16 Mar, pull Tyrrell's child admission price for Leo, and report back with options before booking anything.

I don't have a reliable number for letter mail from Toronto to Mumbai, so I'd rather check than guess. Whatever it is, I'd post the card early to be safe.
Action: look up Canada Post's current delivery estimate for letter mail to India and tell you the latest date to post it for a date you choose.

Good, I'll mark those 3 unmatched charges as yours. I don't have the bakery or cake details saved, so I'll start from your email.
Action: search your email and receipts for the earlier cake order (bakery, size, flavour), check they can do it for New Year's Eve, and show you the order before placing it.

Here's a draft text: 'Thank you so much for the shortbread, Hannah! Leo ate four, so I think that counts as a review.'
Action: wait for your edits or go, then send it to Hannah.

I'll pull every open payouts ticket from Linear, group them by workstream, and flag what looks at risk for December based on status, owners, blockers and due dates. I'll separate what's a fact from what's my judgment call.
Action: pull the open payouts tickets, group by workstream, and send you the grouping with an at-risk list.

I don't have a note on what Leo's been obsessing over lately; the only recent thing I know is the couch-cushion fort that Biscuit has claimed. I'd rather not guess for Grace, and I don't have his food restrictions in front of me either, so I wouldn't tell her what to skip without checking.
Action: search your notes and messages for Leo's current interests and any food restrictions; if nothing turns up, I'd suggest you or Sam tell Grace directly.

Biscuit has real power-tool energy for a beagle, and Diego now thinks you have a contractor in the house.
Action: none needed.

Setting the Sunday call: a recurring slot with your mother Anjali at 9:00 am Toronto time (6:30 pm in Mumbai), marked busy so I never schedule over it. For Spanish, I'd suggest short role-play chats between lessons, 10 to 15 minutes, where I play a real situation and correct you at the end; tell me which days work.
Action: create the recurring Sunday 9:00 block (I'll hold an hour unless you want a different length) and wait for your days and focus areas for the Spanish practice.

I don't have your trip dates or the city your mom is in in front of me, so I can't answer the timing or the rain question properly yet.
Action: check your calendar and email for your booking to see her, then use her city to work out the time difference (so you know if it's too late to call now) and the forecast for your dates, and send you a short reply you can pass to her.

Welcome back, a long-weekend drive plus a Tuesday start is a rough combination. Coffee first, and I'll keep the list light until you're ready.
Action: nothing yet; say when you want a quick rundown of the day.

I don't have your packing method saved anywhere I can see, so I won't guess at it. For the trip home (AC120 YVR-YYZ, Mon 13 Jul, 13:15) I can build a checklist that already includes Leo's swim shirt and his stuffie and builds in time for a long bag wait.
Action: draft a return-trip packing list with those lessons built in, and ask you how you like packing done (per-person lists, when to start, carry-on versus checked) so I can save it for future trips.

Congratulations on the half marathon, 2:04:37 on the Toronto waterfront is a huge first, and Marcus clearly earned his dragging rights. Set up: a recurring Friday 15:00 reminder to post the payouts status in #payouts-launch by 16:00, five bullets with red/amber/green per workstream, pre-drafted from Linear; and Friday evenings held clear for pizza and movie night.
Action: create the Friday 15:00 reminder, block Friday evenings as busy (what hours should I hold?), and save your race result to your notes.

Tom's question can wait until after dinner; I'll leave it unanswered. One flag: my notes say your library card expires 2026-02-14, so if that date has passed I'll check it was renewed.
Action: check your Toronto Public Library account (card ending 4417) for ready holds at Pape/Danforth and Leslieville and anything due this week, then report back.

I'll book 30 minutes since you asked for a half hour, with the agenda in the invite: negative balances and reversed transfers.
Action: find a slot Mon to Wed when you, Aisha and Diego are all free, send the invite with that agenda, and tell you the time I picked.

I don't have this year's start date for the Leslieville farmers market, so I'll check the market's own site rather than guess.
Action: look up the opening date and hours and send them to you.

Ottawa is roughly a 4.5 to 5 hour drive from Toronto before stops, so leaving right after school pickup on a Friday, with traffic and a break, you'd likely roll in somewhere in the evening; I need the pickup time to be more exact. Also, Friday evenings are your pizza and movie night, so you'd be skipping that one.
Action: check your calendar for the school pickup time, estimate the arrival with live traffic, and ask you whether to move pizza night.

Good things to ask on the tours: staff-to-child ratios and staff turnover, how long the educators have been there, the daily routine and outdoor time, the illness and sick-day policy, how they handle settling in and naps, what fees include, and when a spot would realistically open. Also ask to see the space during a normal hour.
Action: none; I can turn this into a printable checklist note for her.

I don't have the GA date saved, so I'll confirm it before putting it in writing. Draft: 'Hi Olivia, the Instant Payouts GA date is [date]. Let me know if you need anything else for the deck. Best, Riya'.
Action: check Linear and Notion for the GA date, fill it in, and show you the draft before sending it.
